newsitem.title: USA: Dell Internet revs in excess of $1 mln/day.
newsitem.headline: Dell Internet revs in excess of $1 mln/day.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp said Tuesday that sales from its Internet site are generating revenues of more than $1 million a day.
Sales from the site at growing at a rate of 20 percent a month, the company said.
The company's shares rose 1-1/8 to 73-3/4 in late morning trading on Nasdaq.
Dell said its web site, visited by more than 225,000 customers a week, has shown that Internet customers are willing to purchase richly configured systems, including high-end $30,000 servers.

"The Internet is proving to be the ultimate 'direct' medium and the next generation of the direct business model we pioneered...we are using the Internet to evolve the direct model," said Michael Dell, chairman and chief executive.
The site is popular with businesses because it improves transaction efficiencies and reduces overall costs to buy and deploy computer systems, the company said.

Gary Arlen, a veteran online industry analyst who heads Arlen Comuncations in Bethesda, Md., said that Dell's "remarkable" revenue figures for the Internet site underscore the progress made in electronic commerce.
"They are shipping a lot of boxes," he said.
"It recognizes that customers who are comfortable with electronic commerce...that there is no dollar amount barrier," Arlen said.
